nodes.text: TXN-C02-DISPUTED ($11.40 USD, 2026-10-14 08:12Z, card_present) is posted to MER-C02, Bluefern Coffee Roasters (US, MCC 5814). Descriptor DSC-C02-TAPR is 'TAPR* BLUEFERN CAFE BOSTON', describes the disputed transaction on 2026-10-14, and is linked by SUB_MERCHANT_OF to MER-C02; no separate parent/payment-facilitator Merchant is present in the traversed hierarchy. Therefore TAPR* does not graph-resolve to a distinct parent; the supported merchant resolution is Bluefern.

nodes.text: TXN-C02-DISPUTED is consistent with the cardholder's established Bluefern Coffee Roasters activity: the same active Visa card CRD-C02 (ending 0202) was used for two earlier posted card-present purchases at MER-C02, TXN-C02-PRIOR-A ($9.75 on 2026-08-04 08:12Z) and TXN-C02-PRIOR-B ($12.60 on 2026-08-27 08:19Z). The disputed $11.40 purchase occurred at 08:12Z, matching the prior morning pattern; the merchant is the same despite the descriptor changing from BLUEFERN COFFEE ROASTERS to TAPR* BLUEFERN CAFE BOSTON.

nodes.text: P6 / C12: Four not-received claims totaling $1,087.75 show a delivery-ring pattern: four different customers used the same device DEV-C12-SHARED and four orders shipped to the same unit ADR-C12-RING (29 Lantern Court, Queens, unit 1), with door photos and resident signers. The separate C12B claim is not part of that ring: its parcel went to ADR-C12B-WRONG (601 Grove Lane, unit 3C), and merchant evidence was requested but unanswered by the passed deadline, so the delivery proof for C12B is unavailable and the $284.20 claim gets the missing-evidence default.

nodes.text: P4 / C08: Six disputed card-present fraud transactions (TXN-C08-FRAUD-1..6; total $2,697.90) followed six separate cardholders' purchases at the same fuel-pump terminal TRM-C08-PUMP6 within 10 days. The shared terminal is a credible common compromise point; the later fraud transactions themselves have no terminal link, so this supports compromise but does not identify the perpetrator or prove the merchant caused it.

nodes.text: P5 / C11: The C11 fraud series is consistent with account takeover, not ordinary household use: one prior undisputed purchase used DEV-C11-OLD, while 40 disputed online purchases from 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-18 used the novel DEV-C11-NEW and hosting/VPN IP-C11-VPN, all at Orbital Audio. The timing and shared infrastructure support one coordinated actor; no SAME_ACTOR edge is present in the graph, so SAME_ACTOR remains an inference rather than an existing fact.

nodes.text: C13 mandate review: TXN-C13 is a $780 hotel transaction initiated through token TOK-C13 under mandate MDT-C13, which authorizes hotel room only and caps each transaction at $600. The transaction is within the mandate dates but exceeds the cap by $180; it therefore exceeded agent authority, so the disputed amount should not be treated as fully authorized merely because AGP-C13 acted for CUS-C13.

nodes.text: Within the C02-only scope, TXN-C02-DISPUTED is linked to one open fraud dispute, but the card and merchant show a repeated same-card/same-merchant pattern: CRD-C02 was used at MER-C02 on 2026-08-04, 2026-08-27, and 2026-10-14, with the disputed transaction matching the prior morning timing. No C02-linked COMPROMISED_AT, SAME_ACTOR, terminal, device, IP, account-event, or additional dispute linkage was found in the queried period; this makes card/device/terminal/account compromise unsupported, though the dispute itself remains open.

nodes.text: C02 does not support an authorized-household-member or agent explanation for TXN-C02-DISPUTED. ACC-C02 has only CUS-C02 as a primary holder; no additional authorized-user/household holder, C02-linked token, mandate, agent-provider relationship, device, IP, terminal, or account-event record was found. The transaction was card-present on CRD-C02 and matches two prior same-card purchases at MER-C02, which supports routine/repeated merchant activity but does not identify a permitted third-party user. A household-use explanation remains possible only if Hollis Marchetti had permitted someone to use the card, but that permission is not evidenced in the graph.
